title: Clipboard
what: Exactly the locked content: the head (The B2B AI Standard, Open for votes), the two-tone title and the six rows, with row 06 as the only orange link. The form only adds physical parts: a board with visible edge thickness and a rounded rim, two loose sheets under the top one, a stationery clip (riveted base plate, hinge knuckles with spring coil, lever with a hanging hole and rolled lip), and "Open for votes" set as an outlined stamp.
why: A clipboard is the sheet that gets passed around a room: it is open, anyone can pick it up and add a line, and the clip says the page is held for now, not bound and final. The stamp reads as an official mark on a draft that is still taking votes, and the empty last row is the spot left for you.
how: Real 3D inside one tilted rig: the board is a face plus six stacked outlines stepping back 1.4px each, the sheets and the clip sit a few pixels in front, and the lever is an inline SVG drawn in 1px hairlines with tone gradients for volume. On load the board settles down onto its place, the sheet slides up under the open clip, the lever snaps shut with a small overshoot, the stamp lands, then the rows write in left to right (about 1.2s, ease-out, transform/opacity/clip-path only); the pointer tilt from base.js still drives the rig and row 06 lifts 2px on hover/focus. Reduced motion shows the final state with no movement; under 700px the 3D is flattened, the edge thickness becomes outlines offset downward and row 06 keeps a 44px+ target.
